A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with TiDeSPL-VAE renamed TE-ViDS. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data reconstruction experiments, mouse visual-stimulus decoding results, latent visualizations, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds results for unseen stimuli, cortical regions, representational similarity, and additional model controls.

M1.justification: The architecture matches after content/style are renamed external/internal. However, v2 Section 3.2 explicitly includes reconstruction and KL terms for both the sample and its positive partner, whereas v3 writes only the sample terms. The PDFs do not clarify whether this is abbreviated notation or an actual training-objective change.

E1.justification: Natural-scene evaluation expands from five strongest-response scenes to all 118. v3 also adds generalization to unseen scenes/movie frames and regional, pooled-mouse evaluations, including the CEBRA-preprocessed Allen dataset in Appendix K. These extend coverage beyond the original retained-trial experiments.

E2.justification: The principal LFADS, pi-VAE, Swap-VAE, and CEBRA comparators remain. Beta-VAE is removed, and TE-ViDS-small is added as a capacity comparator. LFADS and pi-VAE also join the movie constraint-window and trajectory comparisons where they were previously absent.

E3.justification: The reported training budget changes from 5,000 iterations for scenes and 20,000 elsewhere to more than 20,000 until convergence. New protocols include training on 95 scenes and testing on 23 unseen scenes, smaller-capacity controls, equal 150-neuron regional samples, and a 40-time-step setting in Appendix K. These statements do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds representational similarity analysis, regional comparisons, unseen-stimulus tests, and non-recurrent, External-Only, and Internal-Only model ablations. These single-branch models differ from v2's existing tests that merely decode separate latent subspaces. Earlier shuffle and component analyses remain, while the trial-level scene scatters and Mouse 2–5 scene visualizations are removed.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 2 specifies standard errors from ten random initializations, whereas v2 Table 1 specifies five for temporal synthetic results; additional runs cannot be inferred. Non-temporal individual-run dots become standard-error bars. Appendix ablation displays retain uncertainty marks but lose v2's explicit caption definitions of ten-run standard errors.

E6.justification: The five-scene results are replaced by 118-scene results, and unseen-stimulus, regional, similarity-analysis, and additional ablation results are introduced. The proposed model's movie scores are retained, but Swap-VAE's Mouse 2 score changes from 44.99 ± 0.76 to 51.31 ± 0.73 (v2 Table 3; v3 Table 2). Changed coverage and training statements preclude interpreting these revisions as uniform same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit lower-bound step subtracting the contrastive loss and includes it in the final derived objective. It also corrects the NT-Xent arguments from style variables in v2 Equation 18 to external variables in v3 Equation 16, consistent with the stated contrastive procedure. The remaining sequential ELBO derivation is substantially retained.

C1.justification: The decoding and temporal-representation claims remain, but v3 adds explaining inter-subject variability and providing evidence for cortical functional hierarchy as central contributions. These appear in the abstract, contribution list, and Discussion, substantially broadening the claimed scientific contribution.

C2.justification: New similarity patterns are interpreted through internal-state changes and differences between static and continuous stimulation. Regional results receive hierarchy and multisensory-processing interpretations. The Discussion newly acknowledges that absent internal-state or behavioral measurements prevent quantitative validation of internal latent interpretability; Appendix K also reports region-dependent comparative performance.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code link, GRU depth and hidden dimensions, decoder SoftPlus activation, parameter counts, grid-search ranges, and synthetic positive-pair construction details (Appendices A, E, and F). These substantially expand implementation disclosure without establishing procedural changes. Conversely, v2's explicit inference-history description is no longer provided.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands discussion of recurrent dynamics and behaviorally relevant versus irrelevant representations, including rSLDS, low-rank RNNs, DFINE, and DPAD. New internal-state, representational-similarity, and cortical-organization literature supports the broader biological positioning. This exceeds bibliographic updating; the beta-VAE reference is also removed.

P1.justification: The title, model name, latent terminology, abstract, introduction, and substantial methodological prose are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into separate dataset, metric, comparator, and results sections. Ablations move to Appendix J, while biological analyses occupy the main narrative.

P2.justification: The overview is redrawn with a learning-objective diagram, while the earlier module diagram moves to Appendix A. Synthetic results are consolidated into bar plots; new similarity matrices and regional plots appear. Latent visualizations are reworked, and ablation tables and sensitivity plots are reorganized across tasks and all five mice.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v2's restricted five-scene validation by evaluating all 118 scenes and adding capacity, recurrence, and single-branch controls. Additional generalization tests and implementation disclosures make the evidence more informative and assessable. The unseen-stimulus decoder setup and loss rewrite remain underexplained, and biological interpretations remain indirect, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial strengthening of empirical support.
